dedupe_keys.name: cdc flusurge 2 0 spreadsheet model of hospital surge demand during an influenza pandemic

description: FluSurge is a spreadsheet model that gives hospital administrators and public health officials estimates of the surge in demand for hospital services during an influenza pandemic. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention developed it, releasing version 1.0 in July 2004 and version 2.0 later; its page now sits in the CDC web archive. For a pandemic whose length and virulence the user sets, it estimates hospitalisations and deaths and compares the number of people hospitalised, needing intensive care and needing ventilator support with existing hospital capacity. Users can change the average length of stay, the share of admissions needing an ICU bed and the total number of people hospitalised, and can use 1968 and 1918 style scenarios. Coverage is whatever area the user describes, typically a hospital, county or state in the United States. The Excel workbook with macros is a free download as a US government product and runs on Windows. Caveats: CDC states that its outputs are illustrations for planning, not predictions, the tool is no longer maintained, and child outcome rates are averaged over ages 0 to 18. Simulation uses: quick estimates of bed, ICU and ventilator shortfalls for pandemic surge scenarios, and a transparent benchmark for more detailed hospital capacity models. Related records: the treat-sim discrete event model (model-treat-sim-treatment-centre-des) and Ciw (model-ciw-queueing-network-simulation) model patient flow in more detail, and OpenABM-Covid19 (model-openabm-covid19) simulates epidemics.
